current_text.html: The pastor is, by virtue of his office, the moderator of the Session. In the pastor's absence, if any emergency should arise requiring immediate action, the Session may elect one of its members to preside, the quorum for such emergency meeting being as in the case of a church with no pastor in 12-1. Should prudential reasons at any time make it advisable for a minister other than the pastor to preside, the pastor may, with the concurrence of the Session, invite a minister of the same Presbytery to perform this service.

relationships.title: Relationship of Assistant Pastor to the Church

occurrences.excerpt: An overture detailing how assistant pastors are called was found in conflict with BCO 3-2 and 12-2 through 12-4, as the relationship of an assistant pastor to a congregation is best left to the session.

relationships.title: Meaning and manner of reaffirmation of faith for membership

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that 'reaffirmation of faith' historically means answering BCO 58-5 questions 1 and 2, but a testimony of Christian experience may also satisfy it, and requesting reaffirmation of transferring members is not improper.

presbytery authority to resolve questions of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: Mt. Carmel Session challenged New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution, arguing that the Westminster Standards require six consecutive twenty-four-hour days. The SJC majority concluded that Presbytery could resolve the doctrinal question under BCO 11-4 and that prior Assembly actions permitted latitude on the length of the creation days. The General Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint.

metadata.synopsis: A pastor complained that Presbytery upheld his Session’s refusal to give him financial reports prepared for Session members, while also alleging record-transmission, circularization, factual, and constitutional errors. The SJC denied Specifications 1–5 but sustained Specification 6: because the pastor was a Session member, the Session’s authorization made the reports available to him regardless of whether other elders collected copies. His pastoral relationship had ended, however, so the access claim was moot and conferred no present right to the reports. Reasons for Specifications 1–2 were adopted from Case 90-9.
